FIT SCAN · walk-forward

how to read this

Blocks. After a warm-up long enough for the slowest setting in the grid, the history is cut into five equal blocks, B1–B5 (dotted lines on the chart). Every setting is simulated once over all of it, with the fees, fills, sizing and exit rule from the SIMULATION card.

Walk-forward. B3's setting is picked using B1–B2 only, B4's using B1–B3, B5's using B1–B4. A test block never influences its own pick, so the stitched B3–B5 result is a true out-of-sample estimate of the process “optimise this ticker”. That process is what has to beat the preset. The old scan sorted by its OOS column, which quietly made the OOS period the fitting period.

Rank (skill). Where the walk-forward pick finished among all settings in the block it had not seen. 50% is a coin flip: the in-sample winner did no better than a setting drawn at random. Consistently above ~60% means picking settings carries real information forward.

edge = strategy return minus buy & hold over the same bars, in percentage points. MAR = return ÷ max drawdown (drawdown floored at 1%). blend = rank of edge + rank of MAR, the trend_scan.py criterion. consistency = median of the per-block edges, which punishes a setting that won one block and lost the others.

plateau scores each setting by the median of itself and its eight grid neighbours, with neighbours that miss the trade minimum counted as the worst score. A lone spike is not trusted.

Preset = CONFL 90/1.7 standard · MR Pine preset table (fallback 60/2.0) · TREND trend_scan.py optimised preset. The TREND preset was itself fitted on the first 70% of the history, which overlaps B3–B4, so it is partly in-sample here and its comparison is flattered.

Recommendation = the pick using all five blocks. Its own numbers are in-sample by definition. How far to trust it is what the walk-forward rows measure.

Scan all tickers answers two questions with far more data than one ticker can give. (1) Does per-ticker fitting carry forward? Pooled rank over every ticker's test blocks. (2) Does ONE setting for the whole watchlist, picked on training blocks only, beat the preset in later blocks? Ticker-blocks in the same period move together, so the ± understates the real uncertainty. A pick that holds across all three folds matters more than the z-score.

Extended grid. CONFL adds basis, soft on/off and cooldown 0/3/6. MR adds smoothing 1/4/7/10 and pivot 1/2/3. TREND adds hysteresis 0/0.5/1% and a master SMA 0/100/200. Settings that are not scanned come from the cards. TREND hysteresis and master are chart_lab only: trend_scan.py cannot run them yet.
